 1 / 3 “I miss him”: Kate Middleton gets real about Prince George being away at boarding school!
 Sending your oldest kid off to boarding school is a massive milestone for any parent, and it turns out royalty isn't immune to that empty-nest feeling. The Princess of Wales recently dropped a candid update about family life, admitting she’s been counting down the days until her eldest son comes home for the autumn break.
 During an unannounced stop at Café 98 - a cozy charity shop benefiting a local children's hospice - Kate spent time chatting with well-wishers waiting outside. When a young boy mentioned it was his last day of classes before the break, Kate smiled and shared that her own household was in full pre-vacation mode.
 "My children break up tomorrow, and I can’t wait to have them all home," she said.
 One local woman who chatted with the Princess added a little extra detail, revealing that Kate explicitly mentioned missing 13-year-old Prince George since he packed his bags for school. She teased that the family might even sneak away for a quiet trip together over the holiday.
 by TOI Lifestyle Desk 2 / 3 A new chapter for the Wales household
 This marks the very first time Kate has spoken publicly about George living away from home. While 11-year-old Princess Charlotte and 8-year-old Prince Louis are still day students at nearby Lambrook School, George took a major leap this past September by enrolling at Eton College - the iconic, centuries-old boarding school his father, Prince William, also attended.
 Back on September 8, William and Kate walked alongside George as he arrived on campus for his first day, greeting the school's leadership before the young prince officially suited up in Eton’s signature tailcoat uniform.
 Even though he's living on campus full-time now, Eton isn't far from the family's home at Windsor, making quick visits relatively easy. The school calendar includes brief weekend breaks - known in Eton parlance as "exeats" - where students can head home from Friday afternoon through Sunday evening, meaning George has likely dropped by a couple of times already.
 Education experts point out that the first half of the term at Eton is intentionally intense, packed with team-building activities designed to help the new batch of first-year boys build tight-knit bonds with their housemates. But for parents, that initial adjustment period is rarely easy. Letting go is a huge emotional shift, and even with royal schedules, those secondary school years tend to slip by fast.(Instagram)
 3 / 3 Keeping things grounded
 Inside the café, Kate also mentioned that her parents, Carole and Michael Middleton, were equally thrilled about the upcoming school break. The Middleton grandparents are notoriously hands-on, frequently hosting George, Charlotte, and Louis for sleepovers and weekend get-togethers.
 As Kate simply put it: "Half-term is a good time to catch up on family life."
 Whenever the kids are off from school, William and Kate make a point to clear their public calendars, intentionally scaling back royal duties to focus entirely on family time. It's a deliberate choice that reflects how the couple approaches parenting - blending royal traditions with the normal, grounded upbringing Kate experienced growing up.
 Judging by how eager the Princess is to get all three kids back under one roof, this half-term break couldn't have come soon enough. (Image via Getty)
